case_title: Indrajit Sureshprasad Bind & Ors. v. State of Gujarat
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304B, s.498A, s.306 read with s.114
weapon: Kerosene (poured over the victim's body; self-immolation)
evidence_type: Documentary (letters Ext. 49, Ext. 31, Ext. 44); oral evidence of PW3 and defence witness DW1
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss. 304B, 498A and 306 IPC; sentence not stated in the judgment
neutral_facts: The victim married the accused husband in 2002, and his parents lived with the couple at the matrimonial home in Ahmedabad. On 18 May 2004 the victim poured kerosene over her body and died of burn injuries. Five days later, on 21 May 2004, her brother lodged a complaint with the police. He alleged that the victim had written to him that her husband and in-laws had harassed her for about two years over demands for household items and a colour television, that they used abusive language and beat her, and that they had instigated her to end her life. The brother produced a photocopy of a letter dated 16 February 2004, said to be written by the victim from Ahmedabad, and gave evidence that it was the victim's writing. The defence contended that the victim was at her parents' village in Bihar on that date and produced a postal inland letter bearing dispatch and receipt stamps, together with a witness who had written it, to support this. The brother also produced his own letter of 25 April 2004 to the victim, in which he wrote that after speaking to her on the telephone he was satisfied she was living happily and not being misbehaved with, and referred to sums of Rs.33,000 and Rs.43,000. The police registered an FIR, investigated, and filed a charge sheet.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from burn injuries after pouring kerosene over her body
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (court could not record a definite finding of a dowry demand of Rs.33,000 or Rs.43,000)
motive: alleged: demand for dowry and cruelty/harassment by the husband and his parents; not accepted by the court
key_evidence_accepted: Defence witness DW1's evidence supported by Ext. 44 (inland letter with postal stamps) accepted as making it probable the victim was in Bihar on 16-02-2004; Ext. 31 (letter of 25-04-2004) relied on as showing the victim was living happily and not being misbehaved with
witness_credibility: Court had grave doubts about PW3's account and the authorship of Ext. 49; PW3's own letter Ext. 31 (admitted by him) undermined the cruelty story; DW1's evidence found to be supported by documents
bail_history: Appellants on bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged. Earlier bail history not stated
trial_duration: offence: 18-05-2004; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 04-12-2006; Supreme Court: 18-03-2013
legal_representation: Accused: Haresh Raichura, Saroj Raichura, Kalp Raichura, Ranvir Singh, Rajat Vats. State: Hemantika Wahi, Pinky Behara, Shubhade Deshpande
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial held
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss. 304B, 498A, 306 IPC. High Court: conviction affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, convictions set aside
prosecution_argument: Ext. 31 shows a dowry demand of Rs.33,000 or Rs.43,000 on PW3 in connection with the marriage
defence_argument: Victim was in Bihar, not Ahmedabad, on 16-02-2004, so Ext. 49 is not genuine; victim wanted to stay with her parents and was a minor when married
legal_principle_applied: Prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt cruelty or harassment in connection with dowry soon before death (s.304B) and cruelty as defined in the Explanation to s.498A; mere demand of dowry without cruelty is insufficient; abetment requires proof of instigation
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds of the appellants discharged
